name: Open Items
rows: Fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 · USD · Equipment and leases audit workpapers
DRAFT FOR THE CPA · audit procedures · not an audit report · no opinion

Northline Crane Supply agreement NCS-RA-2291 rents HGC a crawler crane for 36 months from September 1, 2025 at $18,500.00 a month, which HGC may not end early. It is a lease, not short-term, and an operating lease by the five tests. It is expensed as a rental and missing from the lease schedule. Proposed: record a right-of-use asset and a lease liability of $448,826.56 at June 30, 2026 ($199,035.79 current, $249,790.77 long-term), discounted at the policy’s 6.75%. Income is unaffected. The machine never posts.

The office lease was extended 60 months from January 1, 2026 on December 12, 2025. It is an operating lease and must be recognized; the controller only discloses it, at a flat $19,500.00. Recomputed with the 3% steps: lease liability $970,390.27 ($178,748.07 current), right-of-use asset $963,156.48, and rent expense $7,233.79 below the straight-line lease cost for January to June 2026. The disclosure’s liability is $59,363.50 too low as well.

Cascade Iron invoice CIE-26-30612 for the skid steer EQ-4416 includes work order WO-6127, $34,800.00 to rebuild the hydraulic pump and final drives of excavator EQ-3388. Policy 2 expenses repairs. Proposed: credit equipment $34,800.00, debit repairs $34,800.00, and reverse June’s $580.00 of depreciation. Income is overstated $34,220.00. The partner’s request for EQ-4416 approved $127,200.00, which leaves the repair out.

EQ-3388, bought used in January 2020, is on the register at 60 months; Policy 4 says 84 for its class. It was fully depreciated in December 2024 but worked 1,420 hours this year. At 84 months, FY2026 depreciation is $42,857.14 more and accumulated depreciation $21,428.57 less at June 30, 2026; $64,285.71 belongs to earlier years, a correction of an error if the CPA treats it so. The machine never posts.

EQ-4022, Slipform concrete paver, has been idle since September 2025 and was listed for sale on May 18, 2026 at $310,000.00. Net book value $427,800.00. If held for sale, it is measured at $291,400.00 after commission: a $136,400.00 write-down. If not, the partners test recoverability from its expected cash flows. The CPA reads the listing and the partners’ intent and decides.

EQ-4415, GPS survey and layout equipment from Benchline Instruments, $84,150.00 on April 27, 2026, has no capital expenditure request. Policy 5 needs a partner’s signed request before an order over $25,000. The invoice and the equipment are real (it logged hours from April); the control did not work. The CPA considers it for the communication of control deficiencies and asks who ordered it.

Four fully depreciated units still work, among them EQ-2740, the 2012 crawler crane, 1,180 hours this year at its full 10-year class life. Policy 6 asks the controller to review lives each year end; there is no record that it was done. The CPA considers whether the crane life is too short (a change in estimate, going forward).

Materiality is proposed at $350,000.00, 0.5% of the year’s revenue, with performance materiality $262,500.00 and clearly trivial $17,500.00. The engagement partner sets the final amounts for the whole audit.
No management representation letter has been obtained. It should cover the completeness of the lease list, the partners’ intent for the paver and the useful lives.
These are draft workpapers and a draft findings memo for the engagement partner. They are not an audit report and give no opinion. Nothing has been signed, posted or sent.
